bull_bear.body:
- Capital position framed as self-funding: 'CRAR at 16.97% and Tier-I at 15.89%, supporting growth with no near-term capital requirement', with Tier-I capital up ₹1,588 Cr on internal accrual funding a 4.5% increase in risk-weighted assets.
- Total capital funds ₹41,015 Cr at Jun-26 versus ₹39,862 Cr at Mar-26; Tier-II fell to ₹2,612 Cr (1.08%) from ₹3,047 Cr (1.32%).
- Balance sheet at ₹3.93 Lakh Cr, with borrowings reduced to ₹18,166 Cr at Jun-26 from ₹21,159 Cr at Mar-26 while deposits rose to ₹3,20,118 Cr; share warrants subscription of ₹1,549 Cr stands unchanged on the liability side.
- Provision coverage strengthened to 87.37% (excluding technical write-offs) from 74.41% a year earlier; Q1 provisions of ₹317 Cr comprised loan loss ₹274 Cr and standard accounts ₹43 Cr.
- No dividend or buyback policy is disclosed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Granular funding is the stated core of the liability franchise: 'CASA + Deposits < 3Cr' is 85% of total deposits in Q1 FY27, up from 82% in Q1 FY26, with the deck framing deposits as 'up 11% YoY with granular funding at 85% of the book'.
- Remittance market share of 20.34% in FY26 (19.30% FY23, 18.67% FY24, 18.42% FY25), computed by the bank on its own remittances data against preliminary RBI balance-of-payments data; NRE deposits ₹95,710 Cr and NR deposits ₹1,05,123 Cr as of Q1 FY27.
- Retail + SME is held at roughly three-fifths of the book — '(Retail + SME)/Net Advances' at 60.2% in Q1 FY27 (60.9% Q1 FY26), where Retail includes Housing, LAP, Auto, PL, CC & Other Retail and SME includes BuB & CoB.
- Improving granularity on both sides of the balance sheet: Top 20 Borrowers down to 5.4% and Top 20 Depositors to 4.55% of portfolio in Q1FY27, versus 10.03% and 7.09% respectively in Q1FY25.
- Deck labels Q1 FY27 GNPA of 1.52% as 'Highest Ever*' / Net NPA 0.18% as 'Decadal Best' (asterisk: excluding one-off), with sequential comparisons presented on a BAU basis excluding the Q4 FY26 one-off.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [International rating] S&P Global Ratings has assigned the bank its inaugural international issuer credit ratings of BBB-/Stable long-term and A-3 short-term; domestic ratings are AAA on Fixed Deposit, A1+ on Fixed Deposit (short term) and Certificate of Deposit, and IND AA+/CARE AA+ on Tier 2 capital bonds and infrastructure bonds.
- [Group companies] Fedbank Financial Services is a 60.7% subsidiary marketing retail asset products of the bank; Federal Operations & Services (FedServ) is a 100% subsidiary providing operational and technology services from Bangalore, Visakhapatnam, Indore and Kochi; Ageas Federal Life Insurance is a 30% associate JV selling since March 2008.
- [Subsidiary performance] Fedbank Financial Services Q1 FY27: AUM up 34.7% YoY to ₹21,136 Cr, disbursals ₹6,760 Cr (+13.9% YoY), RoA 2.6% and RoE 15.4%, 757 branches across 17 states/UTs, capital adequacy 20.7%, 99.2% of AUM secured, credit cost 0.8%, GNPA 1.6% and NNPA 1.0%.
- [One-off adjustment] The deck repeatedly flags a one-off in Q4 FY26; sequential comparisons and growth metrics are presented on a BAU basis with comparatives adjusted, and several ratio series are marked '(Excl one off)' or '#Excluding one-offs'.
- [Reporting inconsistency] The Net NPA % series differs between slides for Q4 FY26 — the credit-metrics chart shows 0.37 (marked '^Excluding one-offs') while the Key Indicators appendix table shows 0.20.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Federal Bank as a granularly funded, Kerala-headquartered private bank with a dominant NRI remittance franchise, scaling profitability by shifting mix toward secured higher-yielding retail assets (gold, LAP, cards) while keeping 85% of deposits in CASA + sub-₹3 Cr tickets.

open.item: West Asia conflict (escalated late Feb 2026) flagged as principal macro risk; full inflationary/energy pass-through expected in later Q1 FY27, and NR remittance/asset exposure to be monitored.
Credit cost guidance retained at 50-60 basis points (FY26 actual ~56 bps), unchanged for now given ECL transition and West Asia uncertainty.
Growth traction (Y-o-Y up from 8% to 13%) expected to build further in FY27 across chosen focus segments; no specific number given.
Plan to launch about 100 branches in FY27, guided by a data-driven network study; ~39 added in Q4FY26.
Further NIM expansion targeted via multiple levers (CASA mix, deposit repricing into Q1/early Q2 FY27, asset mix); FY26 NIM only ~2 bps below FY25.
Plans unchanged to keep building high-yield/unsecured book (credit cards growing ~23% Y-o-Y, MFI restarted, personal loans restarted) despite geopolitical noise.
Corporate book to grow at early double digits with focus on mid-market NTB (75%+ of acquisitions) and cross-sell/wallet share rather than headline volume.
Target CASA ratio of 36% reaffirmed (currently ~32.9%, up ~300 bps since the journey began).
Cost-to-income guidance kept range-bound at ~53-56% (Q4FY26 reported 52.86%, adjusted ~53-ish); no change to strategy-day guidance.
Newly launched wealth management business (a few months in) to build a mass-affluent franchise and become a key fee driver alongside credit cards and trade/forex.
Objective to continue expanding ROA/ROE toward above 1.5% (FY26 underlying ROA 1.24%, up from ~1% three quarters prior); management declined a firm target.
Full ECL transition impact not yet assessed (guidelines ~2 days old); management to come back with studied numbers, expects impact to be reasonable given robust asset quality.
Working to take other income to closer to 1% of assets (currently 0.8-0.9%).
Gold loan yields believed to have bottomed out and expected to move up, aided by rising fee-to-asset ratio (~85-86 bps).

verdicts.item: Under the incoming MD, margin expansion and greater market recognition flagged as key agenda items post the September 2024 leadership transition.
verdicts.note: 'both ROA and NIMs have reached pre-rate cut levels'; NIM 'expanded to 3.20%, up 2 basis sequentially' - margin-expansion agenda progressing.

verdicts.item: CASA ratio targeted to reach 36% over three years (per strategy document), from ~30% currently.
verdicts.note: 'Our target CASA ratio of 36% stays, right?' 'Why not? ... we are close to 33% now ... 36% is getable' - progressing toward 36%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Credit cost expected to remain in the ~40 bps (40-45 bps) range going forward beyond FY25, subject to growth mix.
verdicts.note: 'our credit cost guidance has been 50 to 60 basis points in the past ... if you take the year, we are about 56 basis points' - above the 40-45 bps committed for FY26-onward. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Intention to return to loan/balance-sheet growth of about 1.5x system growth after the reorientation.
verdicts.note: Rikin: 'both your loan and deposit growth has been below system in FY26'; overall growth ~13% - not the 1.5x-system target (reorientation ongoing). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Not accelerating unsecured lending (MFI flat, personal loans negative) until credit-cost environment stabilizes; focus shifted to mid-yield relatively risk-free segments.
verdicts.note: 'MFI, we have begun to grow again. PL, we have begun to grow again' - caution held through the stress period and is now selectively lifting, as committed.

verdicts.item: Shift of internal and external focus to Average CASA as the key liability metric to drive quality and cost-of-funds improvement.
verdicts.note: 'CASA balances crossed the INR 1 lakh crore mark ... growing 8.26% sequentially and nearly 21% Y-o-Y'; 'CASA ratio improved to 32.94%' - average-CASA focus delivering.

verdicts.item: Multiple margin-management measures introduced (fixed-rate pivot, liability mix, average CASA) aimed at improving NIMs over the medium term.
verdicts.note: 'NIM expanded to 3.20%, up 2 basis sequentially'; 'we have just lost about 2 basis points in our NIM over the entire year ... one of the lowest in the sector' - margin measures worked.

verdicts.item: RBI's 30 September gold-loan guidelines may cause one or two quarters of industry-wide disruption before growth stabilizes; bank states it is compliant.
verdicts.note: 'gold loan portfolio delivered a robust performance once again, growing 26% Y-o-Y ... maintained despite the fact that we were downsizing the book of a specific subsegment to ensure full alignment wit…

verdicts.item: Loan growth expected to get better than the 12% seen in FY25, guided at roughly 1.2x-1.5x industry/nominal GDP growth.
verdicts.note: 'last quarter, Y-o-Y looked 8%. Today, it is looking 13%' - above the >12% base but still below system/1.5x. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Cost-to-income ratio expected to operate around 53% (range 52.5%-53.5%) in the next few quarters; flattish 53-handle over the medium term.
verdicts.note: 'Our cost-to-income ratio improved to 52.86%, down 106 basis points sequentially'; guidance reaffirmed at 53-ish range - within the ~53% guide.

verdicts.item: Objective to minimize NIM impact from repo cuts and keep it near current ~3.12%, but management declined to give a firm NIM number given multiple moving levers.
verdicts.note: 'both ROA and NIMs have reached pre-rate cut levels'; 'we have just lost about 2 basis points in our NIM over the entire year' - NIM impact minimized, now above 3.12%.

verdicts.item: Retail slippages expected to stay in the ballpark of ~INR240 crore per quarter, roughly 55-60% of total slippages, with book slippage below 1%.
verdicts.note: 'they have remained 0.74%, which is low' - book slippage below 1% held; retail ~240 cr figure not isolated. [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 58% guidance hit (20 chains); 5 expired; 14% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident, milestone-touting quarter for Manian's first full year; management was transparent about one-off IT-refund gains vs underlying metrics and cautious on ECL/geopolitical uncertainty while holding guidance.
